title: Slice Parameters
goal: Accept slice references in functions so callers can pass arrays, vectors, or subslices.

sections.text: In other languages you pass dynamic arrays everywhere. Beginners in Rust often write functions that demand `&Vec<T>` or `&String`.
Demanding `&Vec<T>` forces callers to allocate a heap vector even when they already have a fixed array. Accepting `&[T]` works for all three storage types.
Rust automatically converts `&Vec<T>` to `&[T]` through deref coercion. The same principle applies to text. Prefer `&str` over `&String` in function signatures.

sections.caption: One signature handles stack arrays and heap vectors.

sections.text: Accepting slice references keeps your API flexible without forcing callers to make unwanted heap allocations.

explanation: Accept slice references in functions so callers can pass arrays, vectors, or subslices.
